# Hierarchical Ecoregion Stratification (`ecoregions.R`) {#ecoregions}

```{r ch5-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

A gram of dissolved organic carbon or suspended sediment does not attenuate the exact same amount of light everywhere. Humic DOC drained from northern peatlands is darker and more aromatic than autochthonous DOC in arid reservoirs (Spencer et al. 2012; Griffin et al. 2018), and fine clay suspensions scatter light much more efficiently per unit mass than coarse glacial silt (Bowers et al. 2020).

To capture this regional biogeochemical coherence across streams, lakes, and estuaries within a single continental framework, `eco_join()` in `R/ecoregions.R` assigns each monitoring station (`SiteID`) to its nested U.S. EPA / CEC North American Ecoregion across **Levels I–IV** (Omernik & Griffith 2014). Nearshore estuarine stations located slightly seaward of coastline polygons are matched to the nearest coastal ecoregion via `sf::st_nearest_feature()`, guaranteeing a strict **1-to-1** mapping from `SiteID` to ecoregion.

```{r eco-map, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.6, fig.cap = 'Left: U.S. EPA Level III Ecoregions (NA_L3CODE). Right: Top 18 Level III ecoregions ranked by number of simultaneous training matchups, colored by water-body type.'}
eco <- get_eco()
tr <- get_training()

p_map <- eco$eco3 %>% group_by(l3code) %>% summarize() %>% st_simplify(dTolerance = 5000) %>%
  ggplot() + geom_sf(aes(fill = l3code), colour = 'white', linewidth = 0.1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = 'turbo') + theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  ggtitle('(a) EPA Level III Ecoregions')

top_l3 <- get_zone_sets()$L3 %>%
  count(l3code = code, type) %>%
  group_by(l3code) %>%
  mutate(tot = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(dense_rank(desc(tot)) <= 18) %>%
  mutate(l3code = fct_reorder(l3code, tot))

p_bar <- ggplot(top_l3, aes(n, l3code, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TYPE_COLS, name = 'Water-body type') +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom', panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = 'Training Matchups (log scale)', y = 'Level III Code', title = '(b) Top 18 Level III Ecoregions by Sample Size')

p_map + p_bar + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.35, 1))
```

## Minimum Sample-Size Rule (`zone_min = 100`)

Every regional model requires at least **`r P$zone_min` training matchups** (`P$zone_min = 100`) to estimate an ecoregion's parameters independently. At Level III (Model 7), **47 ecoregions** exceed 100 matchups, covering **99.69%** of all continental training data; the remaining 0.31% of observations in sparsely sampled ecoregions fall back to the continental model:

```{r zone-counts, echo = FALSE}
zc <- cache_rds('zone_counts', zone_counts(get_training(), eco))
zc %>% group_by(level) %>%
  summarize(`Ecoregions Present` = n(),
            `Modeled Ecoregions (> 100 obs)` = sum(n > P$zone_min),
            `Training Matchups Covered` = fmt_n(sum(n[n > P$zone_min])),
            `Coverage (%)` = round(100 * sum(n[n > P$zone_min]) / nrow(get_training()), 2)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Ecoregion Hierarchy', 'Ecoregions Present', 'Modeled Groups (> 100 obs)', 'Training Rows Covered', 'Coverage (%)')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = FALSE)
```
